questions.question_text: In right △ABC, ∠B=90°, AC=2√5 cm and AB−BC=2 cm. Find cos²A−cos²C.
questions.explanation: Let the legs be x=AB and y=BC. x²+y²=20 and (x−y)²=4, so 2xy=16 and (x+y)²=36; since x>y, x=4 and y=2. Thus cos²A−cos²C=(x²−y²)/AC²=(16−4)/20=3/5.
questions.source: Trigonometry 04.pdf, PDF page 11; exam/year not stated per item (PYQ status unverified)

questions.question_text: If cosθ=(p²−1)/(p²+1), where p>1 and θ is acute, find cosecθ.
questions.explanation: Treat perpendicular= p²−1 and hypotenuse=p²+1. The adjacent side is √((p²+1)²−(p²−1)²)=2p; therefore cosecθ=(p²+1)/(2p).
